name: FitToolbar
description: A toolbar whose items give way, in named steps and an order the items declare, as the region it sits in narrows: it measures its content in its own width, never the window's. The steps are written on each item as `data-fit-<step>` for its styles. A Base UI Toolbar: one Tab stop, the arrow keys inside.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Groups may move to a line of their own (the `wrap` step) when the row runs out of room. Off for a toolbar that floats over content: a second line would cover it, so its last step is into More.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: If `true`, using keyboard navigation will wrap focus to the other end of the toolbar once the end is reached.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The orientation of the toolbar.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

name: FitToolbarButton
description: A toolbar button that can give way: an `md` Button (ghost unless you say) with an icon and a label, an icon square with its label as a tooltip from `labelOrder` on, a + square with its label as a tooltip from `plusOrder` on, and hidden from `moreOrder` on.

props.name: children
props.description: Its label: its accessible name and, once it has given way, its tooltip.

props.name: collapsedIcon
props.description: An icon shown only once its label has given way (the `label` step), in place of `icon`: a button that reads as text while it has room ("Clear filters") and as an icon (×) once it hasn't.

props.name: icon
props.description: Its icon, which stays when its label gives way. A button with a `label` step needs one (or a `collapsedIcon`).

props.name: labelOrder
props.description: When its label gives way (the `label` step).

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: shows the spinner and blocks activation (click, Enter, Space and form submission) while keeping the button focusable. A busy button is `aria-disabled`, not natively `disabled`, so the focus a press left on it stays there and is still there when the wait ends.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: The spinner's accessible name while `loading`: say what is happening.

props.name: moreItem
props.description: What it is in More's menu.

props.name: moreOrder
props.description: When it moves into More (the `more` step).

props.name: plusOrder
props.description: When it shows as + alone, its icon and label gone (the `plus` step): for the primary action, after the groups have wrapped.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

name: FitToolbarGroup
description: A group of items in one row, a fixed gap apart. A toolbar wraps only between groups, the last first; groups with the same `wrapLine` share a line, any other takes one of its own.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: The group as one button (a Filter button for its filters), shown once it collapses.

props.name: collapseOrder
props.description: When it shows `collapsed` instead of its items (the `collapse` step).

props.name: end
props.description: Pinned at the group's end, outside its scroll, with `overflow="scroll"`: Clear all, as ×, at the end of the filters' line. It changes form with the group's items and keeps the form it took once the group wraps, while the items get theirs back.

props.name: firstLine
props.description: Stays on the first line: it never wraps. The page decides which groups do.

props.name: moreItem
props.description: What the group is in More's menu while it is there (`FitToolbarMoreItems`).

props.name: moreOrder
props.description: When the whole group moves into More (the `more` step), its items together: the sort, the grouping and the view switch of a list's toolbar, folded into one menu. Give the group a `moreItem` for More's menu.

props.name: overflow
props.description: `scroll`: the group takes the rest of its line and scrolls sideways instead of giving way, its items whole, the side that hides more fading. Mark an applied or chosen item `data-active`: it is kept in view.

props.name: wrapLine
props.description: Groups with the same `wrapLine` wrap onto the same line, in their order, a fixed gap apart; a group without one takes a line of its own.

props.name: wrapOrder
props.description: When it moves to a line of its own (the `wrap` step), in a toolbar that allows it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: When `true` all toolbar items in the group are disabled.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

name: FitToolbarMore
description: The toolbar's More as one toolbar item: a ghost ⋯ icon button, shown only while an item is in More, its name as a tooltip. Put it where the items it holds were: on a list's toolbar, before the primary action.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element. Its accessible name and tooltip, in the page's language: "More" by default, in English.

props.name: children
props.description: Its icon: ⋯ by default.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Its menu's trigger, which opens the menu holding `FitToolbarMoreItems`: `<DropdownMenuTrigger />`. It renders it as a toolbar button.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

name: FitToolbarPicker
description: A picker's trigger as one toolbar item (a filter: Assignee, Channel): a PickerTriggerButton with an icon, a label, what is chosen and a chevron, filled `info-soft` once a value is chosen, as an applied filter is (Select › Filters). From `labelOrder` on its label gives way, while its icon, what is chosen and the chevron stay ("# ⌄", "👤 1 ⌄"); its label stays its accessible name, read before the value ("Assignee 1"), and shows as its tooltip.

props.name: children
props.description: Its label ("Assignee"): part of its accessible name and, once it has given way, its tooltip.

props.name: icon
props.description: Its icon, which stays when its label gives way.

props.name: labelOrder
props.description: When its label gives way (the `label` step).

props.name: moreItem
props.description: What it is in More's menu.

props.name: moreOrder
props.description: When it moves into More (the `more` step).

props.name: trigger
props.description: The picker's trigger, which opens its popup: `<PopoverTrigger />`, `<DropdownMenuTrigger />` or a Base UI `Menu.Trigger`. The picker renders it as a toolbar button, so the page nests nothing itself.

props.name: value
props.description: What is chosen: the value ("In progress", "Kirby") or a count (`1`). It stays in view when the label gives way, and follows the label in the accessible name. A count (a number, or a string of digits) is set in Space Mono, as machine-written text; any other value keeps the label's font.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

name: FitToolbarSearch
description: The search field of a list's toolbar: it fills the rest of its line and keeps at least the room its icon and its whole placeholder take (measured, or `minWidth`), so the toolbar's other steps come before it is squeezed. From `collapseOrder` on it is a search icon button at the start of the line, which opens the field in the scope's place, More and the primary action kept at the line's end; the field closes once it is empty and loses focus, or on Esc. A search with text stays open. Put it straight in the FitToolbar, between its groups.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Its accessible name ("Search tasks"): the field's and, once it is an icon, the button's, and the button's tooltip.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The clear button's accessible name ("Clear search"): with it, the field has one at its end once it has text.

props.name: collapseOrder
props.description: When it shows as a search icon button at the start of its line instead of the field (the `collapse` step): the toolbar's last step. Without it, it never collapses.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The text it starts with, when it holds its own.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon at the field's start and on the button: a search icon by default.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: The least it may be, in px, before the toolbar gives way. By default it is measured: what its search icon and its whole placeholder (or, with none, its `aria-label`) take, in the field's own font, so the empty field always shows what it is for.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new text as the person types, clears it or presses Esc.

props.name: suppressPasswordManager
props.description: Add common password-manager ignore hints for non-credential fields where extension overlays would obscure custom UI.

props.name: value
props.description: The text, when the page holds it.

name: FitToolbarSplitButton
description: A split button (Button › Split buttons) as one toolbar item: the main action and its ▾, which opens a menu of other ways to the same result (Create agent and its ▾). The pair takes its steps as a whole: from `labelOrder` on the main part shows its icon alone, from `plusOrder` on + alone, its label kept as its accessible name and tooltip, while the ▾ stays beside it. It never moves into More: a menu item can't hold a menu of its own, and the primary action stays on the toolbar. Both parts are toolbar buttons: one Tab stop for the toolbar, the arrow keys reaching the main part, then the ▾. Props other than these go on the main part.

props.name: children
props.description: The main part's label: its accessible name and, once it has given way, its tooltip.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables both parts, as on `ButtonSplit`.

props.name: groupLabel
props.description: The name of the pair, a `role="group"`, in the page's language ("New agent"): not the main part's name ([Button › Split buttons](../button/button.md#split-buttons)).

props.name: icon
props.description: Its icon, which stays when its label gives way (the `label` step).

props.name: labelOrder
props.description: When the main part shows its icon alone (the `label` step); needs an `icon`.

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: shows the spinner and blocks activation (click, Enter, Space and form submission) while keeping the button focusable. A busy button is `aria-disabled`, not natively `disabled`, so the focus a press left on it stays there and is still there when the wait ends.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: The spinner's accessible name while `loading`: say what is happening.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: The menu part's accessible name and tooltip ("More ways to create an agent").

props.name: menuTrigger
props.description: The menu's trigger, which opens the menu of the other ways: `<DropdownMenuTrigger />`. It renders it as the split's ▾, a toolbar button.

props.name: plusOrder
props.description: When the main part shows as + alone, its icon and label gone (the `plus` step): for the primary action, after the groups have wrapped. The ▾ stays.

props.name: variant
props.description: The Button variant; give both parts the same one.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.
